title: Professional scope and restricted-work triage
audience: Coordinators, supervisors and trained workers who may triage, refer, document or support biohazard and trauma-related work. This lesson does not grant authority to enter, assess, clean, decontaminate, release, transport or dispose of anything in a regulated setting.
learningOutcomes: Separate routine cleaning from trauma-related work using the scope, authority and hazard information available.
Name the approver, source documents, boundaries and unresolved risks in a triage record.
Stop and refer when the authority, the hazard or the competence is not confirmed.

instruction.heading: Scope and restricted work
instruction.body: Routine cleaning and trauma remediation are different jobs. They carry different safety, legal, insurance and waste conditions, so a coordinator has to separate them before a quote is given or a worker is assigned. A client who describes a job as just a deep clean after a serious incident has not established what material is present, so the enquiry stays unverified until a competent assessment says otherwise. Before anything moves forward, confirm who gives access, who has released the site, the insurance position, the training held by the people who would attend and the waste rules that apply. Each open unknown is a reason to pause. The triage record names the approver, the source documents, the boundaries of the work, the unresolved risks and the person who receives the handover.

procedure: Record the request as it was received, including who made it and what they describe.
Classify the request as routine cleaning, specialist remediation, waste transport or possible trauma-related work, and note the reason.
Identify who controls access and whether a written release exists. Do not treat a verbal assurance as release.
List every unknown, including material, extent, insurance cover, worker training and waste route. Mark each as open.
Decline any quote or assignment that depends on an open authority question. Issue a written hold notice that names the missing items.
Send the record to the competent supervisor for decision and file it with the job.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks for a just-a-deep-clean quote after a serious incident at a rental unit. No site assessment exists and no release is on file.
workedExamples.reasoning: The request is classified as possible trauma-related work, not routine cleaning. No quote is issued while the authority and hazards are unknown. A written hold notice lists the missing release, the assessment and the insurer position, and the file goes to the competent supervisor.

workedExamples.situation: A property manager says the police have finished and asks for work to start the next morning.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must the worker check first?
workedExamples.reasoning: The worker asks for the written release from the controlling authority and its boundaries. A manager's statement is not that release. Without it, the worker holds the job and records the reason.

equipmentAndPpe: No PPE decision is made in triage. PPE is set later by the competent assessment and the approved plan.
Triage form, hold-notice template and a contact list for the authorities that may need to be consulted.
Training-only fictional job file for practice.

commonErrors.error: Treating a client's description as a verified scope.
commonErrors.prevention: Record it as an unverified enquiry and list what must be confirmed.

commonErrors.error: Quoting before the authority and insurance position are known.
commonErrors.prevention: Issue a hold notice. Quote only after the written scope and approvals exist.

commonErrors.error: Accepting a manager's verbal confirmation as release.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask for the written release from the controlling party and record its boundaries.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not give authority to enter, assess, clean, decontaminate, release, transport or dispose of anything in a regulated setting. Completing it gives no licence, certificate or clearance.

Under the PCBU duty described by Safe Work Australia, a business must protect workers and others so far as reasonably practicable, and the duty cannot be contracted out. The state or territory regulator confirms which law applies.
Some trauma-related work is restricted to licensed, authorised or specially trained people. Confirm the restriction with the regulator for the state or territory before work is assigned.

qualityStandard: The triage record names the authorised scope, the approver and each unknown for the case provided.
Every quote or assignment is held while an authority, insurance or competence question remains open.
documentationEvidence: Triage record with the classification, the reason and the date.
Written hold notice listing the missing items and the person responsible for each.
Source-document list with the approver for each decision.
summary: Routine cleaning and trauma-related work are different jobs. Triage separates them first.
A client description is an unverified enquiry until authority and assessment exist.
Each open unknown is a reason to pause, not to proceed.

knowledgeChecks.question: A client says a serious-incident property needs only a deep clean and asks for a same-day quote. What is the correct first step?
options: Classify the request as possibly trauma-related, issue a hold notice and refer it for a competent assessment.
Quote the usual cleaning rate to keep the client.
Send a worker to look at the property and decide on the spot.

knowledgeChecks.question: A property manager says the police have finished with a site and asks for work to start tomorrow. What is needed before work is assigned?
options: The manager's verbal confirmation, recorded in the job file.
A written release from the controlling authority and its stated boundaries.
A photograph showing that the site looks clean.

officialReferences.title: Duties of a person conducting a business or undertaking (PCBU)
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03. The PCBU must protect workers and others so far as reasonably practicable; hazards are eliminated where possible and otherwise minimised; for certain hazards a hierarchy of control applies (the page does not list its levels); duties cannot be contracted out. The page does not cover trauma cleaning, waste or PPE rules. Publisher: Safe Work Australia. The state or territory regulator confirms the adopted law.

officialReferences.title: Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (2019)
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03, first 100,000 of 133,773 characters only. Read: section 2.2 (standard precautions apply to all people), section 3.1.2 recommendations 7 and 8 (sharps handled minimally, never recapped, bent or broken, disposed of at point of use in an approved container not filled past its maximum fill line), section 3.1.3 recommendation 12 (spill response with gloves and protective equipment, containment, absorbent removal, detergent cleaning). Healthcare-setting guidance, applied here by analogy. Publisher: National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC).

officialReferences.title: Managing spills of blood and body fluids and substances
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03. Standard precautions and PPE for all spill cleaning; clear up the spill before cleaning the area and do not add liquid to a spill; avoid aerosols; leak-proof bags and containers for waste; sodium hypochlorite generally unnecessary for spill management. Victorian guidance only.

officialReferences.title: Managing exposures to blood and body fluids or substances
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03. First response: remove contaminated clothing, wash with soap and water, flush mucous membranes, rinse eyes gently, report immediately; remove from duty and carry out a risk assessment; medical evaluation with post-exposure prophylaxis where appropriate; document date, time, type and circumstances. Victorian guidance only. The page shows its last update as 2015.

officialReferences.title: Cleaning and waste disposal procedures for infection control
officialReferences.covers: Read via WebFetch on 2026-11-03. Three waste groups (general, clinical, pharmaceutical); clinical waste in biohazard bags shown as yellow; sharps into containers that meet the Australian and New Zealand standards named on the page; clinical and pharmaceutical waste collected by waste companies licensed by the EPA and taken to EPA-licensed facilities. Victorian guidance only.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to enter, assess, clean, decontaminate, release, transport or dispose of anything at a scene or in any regulated setting. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate, clearance or permission to do restricted work. Some of the work described here is restricted to licensed, authorised or specially trained people, and some of it may not be done by a general cleaner at all. Where legal, police, coronial, insurer, property-owner or occupational-health authority applies, that authority must be obtained and recorded before any step is taken. Nothing in this lesson replaces the employer's written procedure, the site-specific assessment or the decision of the competent, authorised party. Where you cannot identify who holds that authority, the answer is to stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop work and refer whenever any of the following is true: the biological hazard is uncertain or the contamination status is unverified; the required authorisation, release or competence is missing; the handling, transport, waste or exposure protocol is unknown; a sharp has been found or might be present; a worker may have been exposed; entry has been offered without written release; a party asks you to certify clearance or unrestricted re-entry. A stop-work decision is not a failure. Restart only after the authorised supervisor has documented the procedure and a qualified review has been completed.
